assessment: This important study combines in vivo and in vitro models to characterise the complex role of CYRI-B, an interactor of the small GTPase Rac1, in controlling pancreatic cancer progression towards a higher proliferative and metastatic stage. The authors demonstrate that CYRI-B reduces the typical hyperactivation of Rac1 in early stages of tumor progression; subsequently, CYRI-B mediates internalization of lysophosphatidic acid receptor 1 (LPAR1) uptake through macropinocytosis, thus regulating chemotactic migration of cancer cells towards lysophosphatidic acid (LPA). This work, based on convincing evidence, will be of broad interest to cell biologists and the signalling research communities.
